text:
No exact published match verified for SASRec plus a causal recent-item residual with a learned sigmoid gate. Closest precedents: [HGN](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.09217) gates recent embeddings via S′=S⊙σ(W₁S+W₂u+b), then applies instance gating, average/max pooling, and additive item–item scoring; this is not a gated SASRec residual. [SLi-Rec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2019/0585.pdf) adaptively fuses long/short interests and ablates fusion components. Neither establishes initialization or normalization for the proposed residual. [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781) already contains residual connections and compares against last-item FMC/FPMC baselines, making additional recency benefits an empirical question.

[GNNO](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.10047v1) is the strongest verified transition-graph negative-sampling precedent: construct a training-only graph with distance-weighted increments 1/k; compute neighborhood Jaccard J(i,j); sample p(j|i)∝exp(J(i,j)) over items satisfying J≤λ. Curriculum λ=min(cq,λmax), initialized at zero, gradually admits harder negatives; high-overlap candidates are excluded as likely false negatives. This is a normalized graph-conditioned sampler, not an explicit uniform/transition-successor mixture. No explicit isolated-node fallback was verified; zero-overlap eligible items have equal weight. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) instead converts suspected false negatives into positives with teacher soft labels and consistency regularization.

Consequently, q=(1−ρ)Uniform+ρTransitionHard, uniform fallback for empty pools, and small-initialized residual gates should be labeled implementation choices. Useful controlled ablations: last-item-only, masked recent mean, fixed residual, learned gate, and identical negative counts. A stronger loss-side alternative is [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192): more negatives plus gBCE to reduce overconfidence.
